findings.finding: The adjudicated route, four active decision artifacts, append-only appeal ledger, three complete shared sidecars, and the canonically serialized current Ezekiel and non-Ezekiel sidecar partitions are bound to the SHA-256 values in this report.

Expanding the 115 decision spans and the 115 chunk spans independently against the canonical eng-web Ezekiel passage inventory yields all 1,273 verses exactly once, in canonical order, from Ezek.1.1 through Ezek.48.35, with zero gap, overlap, or ordering error.

All 230 structured decision-level WEB observations match the canonical translation witness strings exactly. Every decision has one complete-verse opening witness and one complete-verse closing witness, and every chunk preserves the identical observation pair in its convergence-defense record.

All 706 recursively observed structured source_refs sets in the active review packets use the packet's exact active span, one direct eng-web reference, and an exactly paired OSHB and UXLC WLC-family locator. The resulting 1,412 locator objects contain no structured source identifier other than oshb or uxlc.

Every decision and every chunk states that OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC or Leningrad-family evidence rather than independent witnesses. Both original-language span fields equal the active decision span, and the only authority value is translation_textual_order_and_form_evidence_only.

No Ezekiel-specific WEB-to-MT verse crosswalk is pinned in the scoped corrective artifacts, and the active records make no exact WEB-to-MT remapping claim. Coverage and quotations were therefore verified in canonical WEB coordinates; OSHB/UXLC checks verify correlated locator identity and same-span disclosure, not a preferred MT/Greek order or an independently established verse remapping.

No structured P967, LXX or Old Greek, DSS, rabbinic, Second-Temple, or ANE source locator, quotation, reading, or witness ruling appears in the checked artifacts. Mentions of those sources occur as unavailability disclosures, textual-pressure warnings, reception guards, preserved historical dissent, or requests for future specialist review; none is used to invent evidence or select a witness, order, reading, identity, chronology, or theology.

All five held decisions retain a decision-local active appeal and route absent local P967, LXX or Old Greek, DSS, rabbinic, or Second-Temple evidence to independent specialist and human review. Missing source evidence is not converted into a preferred reading or boundary.

Every packet contains exactly the Hebrew/textual, literary/prophetic-cycle, and canonical/retrieval-premortem roles. Every independence scope declares the shared model substrate, counts the mesh as one correlated model voice rather than cross-model votes, denies reviewer-count authority, and requires later independent-model or human evidence.

All 36 relation rows are candidate-only, non-authorizing, and boundary_authority=false. Every referenced decision identifier resolves to one of the 115 active Ezekiel decisions, and no relation establishes witness priority, harmonized chronology, identity, fulfillment, theology, or boundary authority.

Each current shared sidecar contains exactly 11 Ezekiel rows, byte-equivalent after canonical row serialization to reviews/Ezek/sidecar_rows_v2.json. Current non-Ezekiel partitions are separately hash-bound above. Because no pre-install non-Ezekiel partition digest or atomic-installer receipt was available to this fresh checker, cross-time non-Ezekiel byte preservation is not independently claimed by this report.

source_gaps: No scoped local primary P967, LXX or Old Greek, DSS, Syriac, Vulgate, rabbinic, Second-Temple, or ANE corpus was available for witness-level verification.
